react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of the 10 differentially abundant metabolites identified a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of Galactose Metabolism. This consensus emerged across two orthogonal paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (SMPDB and KEGG namespaces, FDR = 1.43×10⁻¹¹) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (p = 3.25×10⁻⁷, rank 1/8) — and was independently corroborated by Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p = 0.028, rank 6/15, overlap = 10/11 metabolites). The four driver metabolites are sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and galactinol (KEGG:C01235). InChIKey block-14 reconciliation confirmed all four as structurally distinct, ruling out namespace artefacts. No cross-tool disagreement required reconciliation. Secondary pathway hits include Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (Mummichog rank 3, p = 0.009) and the broad Biochemical Pathways map (RaMP FDR = 1.5×10⁻⁴), both consistent with a primary carbohydrate-processing defect. The secondary Mummichog hits Glycerophospholipid metabolism and Urea cycle/amino group metabolism reflect additional signals from 16(R)-HETE (a cytochrome-P450 arachidonate derivative, KEGG:C14778) and beta-alanine (KEGG:C00099) respectively, but these were not supported by the ORA tools, suggesting they are weaker or indirect signals. The convergent Galactose Metabolism finding is biologically coherent: sucrose dysregulation drives galactitol accumulation via aldose reductase, myo-inositol is interconnected through the galactinol biosynthetic node, and all four metabolites lie within the Leloir pathway and its immediate connected pools. The remaining six input metabolites (allysine, cortisol, D-glucose, silica) did not drive any significant pathway hit and may represent treatment-specific background variation.

MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00052 at the top with p = 6.58×10⁻⁸, matching all four driver metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis confirmed the same four metabolites within its Galactose metabolism module (p = 1.68×10⁻⁴) and additionally retrieved D-glucose (C00221) as a connected hexose-phosphorylation compound. No InChIKey block-14 reconciliation conflicts were observed across the driver set, confirming they represent four structurally distinct entities. Beta-alanine, allysine, cortisol, 16(R)-HETE, and silica did not appear in any significant pathway hit and may reflect treatment-specific background variation. react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of 10 differentially abundant metabolites identified a single dominant signal converging on Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:hsa00052). RaMP multi-database ORA returned this pathway with FDR = 1.43×10⁻¹¹, the strongest hit among 15 pathways, driven by four metabolites: sucrose (C00089), galactitol (C01697), myo-inositol (C00137), and galactinol (C01235). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00052 at the top with p = 6.58×10⁻⁸, matching all four driver metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis confirmed the same four metabolites within its Galactose metabolism module (p = 1.68×10⁻⁴) and additionally retrieved D-glucose (C00221) as a connected hexose-phosphorylation compound. No InChIKey block-14 reconciliation conflicts were observed across the driver set, confirming they represent four structurally distinct entities. Beta-alanine, allysine, cortisol, 16(R)-HETE, and silica did not appear in any significant pathway hit and may reflect treatment-specific background variation. The six galactose-related metabolites collectively indicate a coordinated perturbation of galactose catabolism and its connected inositol and polyol pools, with sucrose and galactinol functioning as upstream substrates and galactitol accumulating as a downstream polyol product.
